text: When should you prefer a `while` loop over a `for` loop?
choices: When performance matters, since `while` compiles to fewer bytecode instructions.
When the loop body may need to modify the loop variable, which `for` forbids.
When there is no natural counter — the loop runs until a condition changes for reasons other than counting.
When the number of iterations is known in advance, since `while` is clearer for fixed counts.
explanation: `for` gathers initialisation, test and update into one line, which is exactly right when they are all about a counter and misleading when they are not. Euclid's algorithm, reading until end of input, and iterating until convergence are all `while` loops — there is a condition and no count. Putting unrelated work into a `for` header is a way of hiding it.
